violation_type.title: AP Infants Sleep on Backs or Must Have Completed and Signed Sleep Exception Form for the Infant (26 TAC §746.2427)
violation_type.short_title: AP Infants Sleep on Backs or Must Have Completed and Signed Sleep Exception Form for the Infant
violation_type.typical_finding: In the infant classroom, there was a 3 month child asleep that was placed on there tummy who is not independently able to roll on there back.     CI: This was corrected at the inspection as the child was place on there back.

finding_variants.text: In the infant classroom, there was a 3 month child asleep that was placed on there tummy who is not independently able to roll on there back.     CI: This was corrected at the inspection as the child was place on there back.
During my walk through, an infant was observed sleeping In a crib with a wedge underneath the mattress. There is no infant sleep exception form on file nor in the classroom with the child.
There was a child observed sleeping on their stomach without being able to independently roll over. The caregiver supervising reported that the infant prefers to sleep on their stomach.

During inspection on 06/14/2024, the inspector observed a six-week-old infant sleeping face down and there was no sleep exception form available for review. Note: this was corrected when infant was moved face up.
At the time of inspection one infant with a wedge under the mattress without a sleep exception form on file.    The wedge was removed.
It was determined in an investigation that an infant was placed face down (on their stomach) in the crib.
